newsitem.title: USA: Time Warner sees oper cash flow growth.
newsitem.headline: Time Warner sees oper cash flow growth.

text.p: Time Warner Inc Chairman and Chief Executive Gerald Levin said Wednesday the company expects to post double-digit growth in operating cash flow.
Levin said the company was aiming to accelerate operating cash flow to "superior double-digit performance not just average double-digit performance."
The increased free cash flow is to be used to pay down debt, which now stands at $17.5 billion, and to eventually buy back its shares, he said in a briefing with reporters.
Levin would not say what kind of pace in debt reduction he expects, or when the company plans to begin buying back shares.
Chief Financial Officer Richard Bressler said the company expects to lower its debt-to-cash-flow ratio to 3.75 by the end of the 1997. The ratio stood at 4.1 at the end of 1996, he said.

Time Warner on Wednesday reported a first quarter net loss of $43 million, or $0.08 per share, on revenues of $3.03 billion versus a net loss of $153 million, or $0.39 per share, on revenues of $2.07 billion.
The per share figures beat analysts' mean estimate of a loss of $0.32 per share.

The improved results came several months after Time Warner completed its merger with Turner Broadcasting Systems. Levin said the company is begining to reap the benefits of creating a varied media company that includes cable, film and television.
"In so many different ways, the Turner properties are helping us accelerate our growth," Levin said.
With the Turner merger behind it, the company has no further plans for acquisitions, he said.
Instead, the company is focusing on making all the various divisions work to build partnerships that feed off one another, he said.
For example, the movie "Space Jam," and its soundtrack were able to cross-promote the two products.
"My focus is on driving the growth of the businesses," Levin said.
((-- Lisa Marie Pane, New York newdesk, 212-859-1713))
